citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility was past due for its regularly scheduled visit by the Attending Veterinarian, as the last visit was performed in
May 2025. This was confirmed by the licensee and after reviewing the Program of Veterinary Care – which stated visits
would be performed “annually”. Missing these scheduled visits results in inadequate veterinary oversight of the licensed
operation. Each dealer and exhibitor shall employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. In the case of a
part-time attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal arrangements shall include a written program of
veterinary care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises of the dealer or exhibitor.
Correct by: July 28, 2026

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee did not follow the intestinal parasite schedule established by the attending veterinarian in the Program of
Veterinary Care. The PVC requires the goats and sheep have “quarterly fecal exams and dewormed every 3 months as
needed”, and for the pigs to be dewormed annually. Not following this schedule compromises preventive health care and
risks untreated parasitic disease that could negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals. Each dealer or
exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include the use of appropriate methods to
prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
Correct by: Correct by: July 28, 2026

The licensee did not have complete and up to date inventory, acquisition, or disposition records for regulated animals,
including pigs, goats, guinea pigs, zebu, and sheep. Failure to maintain accurate and current records prevents verification
of animal traceability and regulatory compliance.
Every exhibitor shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the following
information concerning animals other than dogs and cats, purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or
otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise
disposed of by that exhibitor. The records shall include any offspring born or hatched of animal while in his or her
possession or under his or her control, to the extent that any identification or counting of offspring can be carried out
without unduly disturbing nesting or rearing activities: 1. The name and address of the person from whom the animals
were purchased or otherwise acquired; 2. The USDA license or registration number of the person if he or she is license or
registered under the Act; 3. The vehicle license number and State, and the driver’s license number (or photographic
identification card for nondrivers issues by a State) and State of the person, if he or she is not license or registered under
the Act; 4. The name and address of the person to whom an animal was sold or given; 5. The date of purchase,
acquisition, sale, or disposal of the animal(s); 6. The species of the animal(s); and 7. The number of animals in the
shipment.
Correct by: Correct by: July 28, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
